newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO-Israeli hold contacts, but deadlock stays.
newsitem.headline: PLO-Israeli hold contacts, but deadlock stays.

text.p: Israel and the Palestinians held secret crisis talks overnight but failed to ease a two-month-old deadlock, the PLO said on Tuesday.
It said Israel had rejected Palestinian demands to discuss freezing Jewish settlements on occupied lands.
"Nothing came out of the meeting yesterday," Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's spokesman Marwan Kanafani said.
He told Reuters Israeli representatives "refused to discuss freezing of settlements. As long as they refuse to talk about settlements there is no common ground."

Talks between Israel and the Palestinians were plunged into crisis in March, when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing government broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem.
"They merely want to go back to negotiations to talk about other issues, but nothing even tangible," Kanafani said of the Israelis.
Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak declined comment on the contacts.

Last week a mediation mission by U.S. President Bill Clinton's special envoy Dennis Ross foundered in part on Israel's refusal to agree to curbs on construction in settlements, where some 130,000 Jews live scattered among the two million Arabs of the West Bank and Gaza.

An Israeli newspaper said on Tuesday the United States, Israel's main ally, believed further settlement building to be unnecessary, because U.S. data showed more than a quarter of settler homes in the West Bank were empty.
Israel occupied East Jerusalem in 1967 and claimed the whole city as its capital. The claim is not recognised internationally. Palestinians want East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state.
